newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OMV Q1 net profit falls 6.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: OMV Q1 net profit falls 6.7 pct.

text.p: Austrian oil and chemicals group OMV said on Tuesday net profit in the first quarter fell 6.7 percent to 804 million schillings while pretax profit tumbled 10.7 percent to 912 million schillings.

Reporting final earnings for the first quarter, the country's biggest industrial group confirmed that earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) rose to 1.016 billion schillings from 945 million in the first quarter of last year.
OMV also confirmed that sales, excluding petroleum taxes, climbed over 20 percent to 21.41 billion schillings.

Pretax profit declined nearly 11 percent from the 1.02 billion schillings posted in the first three months of 1996 largely due to a higher interest charge because of the provision for pensions, OMV said in a statement.
Net profit was also weighed down by a higher tax charge.

"The tax charge increased to 0.22 billion (against 0.16 billion in the year-ago period) due to the continuing effect of the non-deductibility of tax loss carry forwards and the proportion of profit generated in Austria," OMV said.

OMV gave no outlook for the full year, but earlier this month, when reporting provisional first quarter earnings, said it expected to see a positive earnings development for the current year. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12256
